contents.Prop 2.1-2.3: Instability iff a strict positive subsolution phi on the link with Delta_S phi >= lambda phi, phi_nu + H phi >= 0, lambda >= (n-2)^2/4.
contents.Sec 3: v = w^alpha, w=||D^2u||; Simons-type interior inequality w Delta w >= 2/(n-1)|grad w|^2 + 2(n-2)/(n-1) w^2/|x|^2; boundary inequality (1/H)(log v)_nu >= -alpha L, L = max(2 + sum u_kk^3/(H w^2)).
contents.Sec 3.2 obstruction: Need (n-2)^2/(4(n-1)) <= alpha <= 1/L; the lower bound is nearly optimal when D^2u has one negative and equal positive eigenvalues, the upper bound when one tangential eigenvalue is positive and the rest negative - 'individually nearly optimal but achieved for different configurations', so insufficient for n<=6; L* = infinity for n>=5.
contents.Sec 4: w^2 = sum_{lambda>0} lambda^2 + a sum_{lambda<0} lambda^2 with a=4 settles n=4.

candidates.name: Flux pair (h = w^a sqrt f, Z = w^{2a}(G:X + wM + P)) with the universal equivariant tensor certificate (f,U,K,M,P; Prop 4.1)
candidates.statement: There exist rational O(5)-equivariant tensor polynomials f,U,K,M,P in (A,p,g) (A unit STF 5x5, g^2+|p|^2<=1) such that, with G = delta U + (K - K^(12)), h = w^a sqrt f and Z = w^{2a}(G:X + wM + P), on any smooth link of a nonflat one-homogeneous Bernoulli solution in S^5: div Z >= |grad h|^2 + 4h^2 + eps_* w^{2a} and N.Z + H h^2 >= delta_* w^{2a+1}; combined with stability this is a contradiction.

test1.verdict: No near-equivalent found. Nearest object: JS 2015 (named, scalar subsolution). Nearest method: SOS auxiliary functions in fluids/control. The combination (non-gradient flux in normalized jets + 4th-derivative/parity elimination + exact equivariant tensor SOS) was not found anywhere before 2026-09-24.

test2.evidence: Judged against the problem as posed (no witness: this is a nonexistence result). Neither f,U,K,M,P nor Z occurs in the goal (flatness of minimizing cones) or in L. JS's w^alpha is in L and h contains the factor w^a but sqrt f(A,p,g) and the flux are not subterms or unfoldings of any L statement; JS's subsolution criterion corresponds only to the special case Z = h grad h with f depending on eigenvalues of A alone.

final.justification: Passes tests 1-3 on searches named above: no near-equivalent object, non-analytic, fully load-bearing. Not a templated strengthening (no induction). Downgrade risks are real: (i) the paper names JS's Hessian-function tests as the precedent and C1 is, conceptually, 'JS with a flux and a computer search'; (ii) the meta-method is an import (SOS auxiliary functions), so a strict judge could call the IDEA N2 and the OBJECT a search output; (iii) correctness rests on unrefereed, uncompiled-in-Lean, code-verified arithmetic with tight margins. Kept at N3 because the specific ansatz that makes a certificate exist (non-gradient flux, g/p dependence, 4th-derivative and parity elimination) has no neighbour and resolves an 11-year-old named obstruction.

family_D.label: D3 (provisional)
family_D.rests_on: C1 alone (flux pair + universal tensor certificate). C2-C4 are N2 design constraints of C1; C5 and everything else N0-N1.
family_D.falls_to: D2 if (a) P-C1 directed or tool arm exceeds the calibrated threshold (an SOS-literate model told JS's obstruction may well propose 'flux + polynomial ansatz + SDP'); (b) a free-boundary or minimal-surface expert identifies a prior flux/SOS certificate for cone stability (none found); (c) judges treat 'JS's Hessian-function test, generalized and machine-searched' as a variant of the named precedent (N2 rule). Moot if the certificate is wrong.
family_D.not_transfer: The meta-method (SOS certificate of an integrated inequality) is imported from polynomial optimization/fluids; the eureka claim rests on the specific geometric ansatz, not on the import. Transfer alone would give D1-D2.
family_D.correctness_caveat: Unrefereed; the new half has no Lean; Prop 4.1 rests on Python exact arithmetic (two engines, 1714/1714 keys agree) whose formula-to-code correspondence the README itself disclaims; margins are tight (D0/Dbar ratios up to 0.99992). Implicitly also proves the CJK smooth-link stability conjecture in dims 5-6, which FR-Serra (Sep 2026) still treated as open.
family_D.compression_note: Not measured. C1 is single-use and bottleneck-shaped; its value is qualitative (breaks JS's dimension barrier), not a measured proof-size blow-up. Downstream-speedup test: natural held-out targets are stable cones for Alt-Phillips, capillary and thin one-phase problems, and the stable-minimal-cone Simons bound.

common.judging: Two-level: (i) IDEA hit, judged by two LLM judges + one free-boundary expert with 367's precedent remarks (history.tex:64-122) and the JS text: proposal must contain (a) a NON-gradient vector field Z with pointwise interior inequality div Z >= |grad h|^2 + 4h^2 (+ positive mass) and boundary inequality N.Z + H h^2 >= 0, (b) built from normalized jets (A=T/w, p, g, grad T/w), (c) with undetermined 4th-order / even-normal jets eliminated by construction, and (d) a plan to certify by SOS. (ii) OBJECT hit (tool arm only): an explicit certificate verified by exact arithmetic for m=5 (any degree).
common.controls: Positive: Cook-Reckhow ER extension variables for PHP. Negative: C5 suspension (expect high hit rate), P35 weighted Bochner (expect near-100%), JS's w^alpha (in L). Sanity control for the tool arm: the same search for m=6 (S^6, Hardy constant 25/4) must FAIL, since the De Silva-Jerison cone is stable in R^7; a 'certificate' for m=6 flags a broken checker.

open_questions: Run verification/checks/reproduce.py in an isolated sandbox (Python -I, copied tree) and, better, re-derive the 1714-key expansion with an independent CAS from the LaTeX only; the margins are tight.

Does the paper use minimality anywhere after Section 2? If not, it also proves the CJK stability conjecture for smooth-link cones in dims 5 and 6 - ask experts (Jerison, Savin, De Silva, Fernandez-Real, Serra) whether that is believed and whether the certificate is plausible.
Falsification test: the same ansatz must be infeasible on S^6 (Hardy constant 25/4) because the De Silva-Jerison cone is stable in R^7. Run the SDP at m=6.
How was the certificate found (SDP solver, ansatz degree, number of iterations)? Not disclosed; affects Test 4 framing (search vs insight).
Is there a much smaller certificate (lower degree, fewer rows)? A small one would strengthen the 'eureka' reading; a necessarily huge one suggests search.
